Both Ends of It
Click 🎧 to listen.
Listen to a conversation between two students. The boy is discussing his opinion about how their theatre group should stage the confession scene. Listen carefully. You will hear the conversation only once. After listening, you will answer four questions about the conversation and the evidence the boy gives to support his opinion. As you listen, you may take notes.
Listen to the Conversation
1 QUESTION 1:
Why does the boy mention the way the booth faces the audience right now?
2 QUESTION 2:
Where did the boy get the idea to open the booth and seat the audience on both sides?
3 QUESTION 3:
What does the boy say happened when the group ran the scene facing Sofia on Tuesday?
4 QUESTION 4:
What does the boy mean when he says the audience would be "sitting inside the family, on both ends of it"?
Answer all 4 questions to submit.
Choose the best answer for each question. You may change your answers before submitting.
SMART SUPPORT:
Go back to the conversation. Identify why the boy brings up the way the booth faces now. Identify where he learned the idea. Identify what the Tuesday run-through showed. Identify his main point about the audience.
